- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 82.31) — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too high and then correcting.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion or lag in capturing late-period momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true price movements, missing volatility spikes and sharp reversals.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices, particularly when historical mean is rising — adjust downward by 2–5% for long-term forecasts.
- When true price rises sharply, model lags by 1–3 days — correct by adding 1–2 days of lagged price momentum to forecast.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices — if last 5 days are above 80, reduce forecast by 3–7% to account for mean reversion.
- For forecasts with early spikes, cap forecast at 10% above the 30-day moving average to prevent runaway overestimation.
